findings.reason: the done-when measures nothing as written; the fixture must hold the state that actually reaches the lock (a live pointer with a declared external wait whose probe has answered, or a run owing a review so the sweep's review pass dispatches), and naming that state is what makes the negative control able to fail.
findings.text: the done-when builds its red/green pair on "two delivered runs", but `resumption.sweep` iterates live pointers and skips each one at `if wait is None and refusal is None: continue` (reckon/crew/resumption.py:2197) before reaching any of the five `_pointer_lock` sites the same section calls likeliest; a delivered run declares no external wait and folds no `_stream_refusal_block` (reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py:615 returns None for a run with no budget refusal), so neither arm of the test takes a lock — the head assertion "no pointer lock is held" holds on the unfixed code, and "with the lock-holding call restored the same acquisition times out" cannot fire because the restored call is never executed.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/station.py` near line 273 is `self._start(lambda: self._run(...))` at exactly station.py:273, `reckon/crew/resumption.py`'s five sites resolve at exactly 217, 232, 1581, 1893 and 1920, and the acquirer list is complete against `grep -rln _pointer_lock reckon/` (the only modules it omits, `reckon/crew.py:116` and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:175`, re-export the name and do not acquire it).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the fixture named by the done-when ("a temporary crew home holding two delivered runs") acquires no pointer lock on any arm, so the assertion "no pointer lock is held" passes on the unrepaired code and the "restore the lock-holding call" control has no call to restore.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the dump, the gate log and the per-arm test logs are named as living "under the run directory", which survives the run; nothing is written to a node-local scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filename and the §48 prose name the mechanism (a station pass holding a run's lock) with no plan label, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — same defect as done_when-1, seen from the third check: the caller the plan designates as "the likeliest holder", a station sweep thread running `resumption.sweep`, returns before acquiring any pointer lock when no live pointer declares an external wait and records no stream refusal, so the mechanism the plan describes is not reached by the fixture it names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — naming the holder and stopping the station holding a run lock are one goal, judged by one verdict (the test's head/control pair), and both are carried by the same gate.
